_note: Fixed parts for motions on Young Lancashire Voice. A motion is four small numbers (subject, reason, action, money), so a link can carry a motion but can never carry typed words. Read by the Young Lancashire Voice page and by the Lancashire Voice page wrapper. Keep every subject within what a county council decides, and keep figures out: a published figure needs a source.

subjects.name: Crossing the road to school
notes: children should be able to walk to school safely
busy roads near schools worry pupils and parents
more children would walk to school if crossing the road felt safe
actions: look again at every primary school that has asked for a crossing patrol
ask pupils which crossings near their school feel unsafe, and publish what they say
put school crossings at the front of the queue for road safety work

subjects.name: Potholes on the way to school
notes: potholes are dangerous for children on bikes and scooters
pavements and cycle paths get less attention than main roads
a safe route to school matters as much as a smooth road for cars
actions: repair potholes on walking and cycling routes to schools first
let pupils report a pothole on their route to school in a simple way
check the routes to one school in every district each year, with pupils

subjects.name: Libraries
notes: a library is a free, warm and safe place to go after school
many libraries close before young people can get to them
teenagers need somewhere quiet to study that is not home or school
actions: open one library in every district later on a school night
set aside a space for teenagers in the larger libraries
ask young people to help choose what their library offers

subjects.name: Things to do
notes: young people need safe places to meet their friends
there is less to do in some towns than in others
a good youth club can change how a young person feels about where they live
actions: run a youth club night in every district each week
ask young people in each district what they want from a youth club
publish a simple list of things to do for young people in every town

subjects.name: Shops selling vapes to children
notes: it is against the law to sell vapes to under 18s, and some shops still do
pupils see vaping in and around school
shops that keep to the law should not lose out to shops that break it
actions: carry out more test purchases at shops that young people report
give young people a simple way to report a shop to Trading Standards
tell the public each year how many shops were checked and what was found

subjects.name: Buses
notes: young people rely on buses to reach school, college, work and friends
the cost of the bus stops some young people going out at all
evening and weekend buses matter most to people too young to drive
actions: ask young people which bus journeys they cannot make now
put young people's journeys first when deciding which bus services to support
publish one simple guide to young people's bus fares in Lancashire

subjects.name: Country parks and footpaths
notes: Lancashire's countryside belongs to young people as well
some footpaths are hard to use or hard to find
being outdoors is good for how young people feel
actions: invite schools and youth groups to help look after a footpath or country park
make it easier to report a blocked or broken footpath
mark one easy walk from every town for families and young people

money: by spending less on something else, which the motion names
by doing it in a few places first to see what it costs
from money the council already has for this service, spent in a different order
